title: When Memory Becomes Authority: Benchmarking Authority Collapse at the Memory Consolidation Boundary
title_zh: 当记忆成为权威：在记忆整合边界基准测试 Authority Collapse
abstract_en: Persistent memory allows (self-evolving) LLM agents to adapt across tasks by consolidating heterogeneous interaction histories into reusable facts, preferences, observations, and rules. Yet consolidation also imposes an implicit authorization boundary: it determines whether stored information may later be consumed as a user fact, an attested observation, or a standing instruction. We identify authority collapse, in which consolidation preserves a claim while erasing the source constraints governing its authorized use, causing the stored memory to imply greater authority than its source permits. We introduce AuthMem-Bench, a controlled paired benchmark that holds the focal claim and downstream task fixed while varying only source authority. It evaluates write-time collapse, downstream authorization errors, and automatic authority preservation. Across seven consolidators based on widely used agent-memory systems and seven LLM backbones, we observe authority collapse in 48 of 49 evaluated configurations. In a controlled action-grounded evaluation, collapsed memories without authority metadata yield a mean unauthorized-action rate of 50.3%. In an end-to-end evaluation, automatically predicted and persisted authority labels reduce the observed unauthorized-action rate from 16.9% to 0.0%, while benign task success remains essentially unchanged. These findings show that memory-driven adaptation must preserve not only what was learned, but also the authority under which it may be reused.
abstract_zh: 持久记忆使自演化 LLM agents 能够通过将异构交互历史整合为可复用的事实、偏好、观察和规则来跨任务适应。然而，记忆整合也隐含了一条授权边界：它决定存储信息之后能否被当作用户事实、经证实的观察或长期指令来使用。本文识别出 authority collapse 现象，即整合过程保留了某个主张，却抹去了约束其授权使用的来源信息，导致存储记忆暗示出高于原始来源许可的权威性。作者提出 AuthMem-Bench，这是一个受控的成对基准，在固定核心主张和下游任务的同时，仅改变信息来源的权威级别，用于评估写入时的权威坍塌、下游授权错误以及自动权威保留能力。对基于常见 agent-memory 系统的 7 种 consolidators 和 7 个 LLM backbones 的实验显示，49 种配置中有 48 种出现 authority collapse。在受控的 action-grounded 评估中，缺少权威元数据的坍塌记忆导致平均 50.3% 的未授权动作率；在端到端评估中，自动预测并持久化 authority labels 可将未授权动作率从 16.9% 降至 0.0%，同时基本不影响良性任务成功率。研究表明，记忆驱动的适应不仅要保存“学到了什么”，还必须保存“在何种权威下可被复用”。
key_points_zh: 提出 authority collapse：记忆整合保留内容但丢失来源授权约束，使低权威信息在后续被误当作高权威指令或事实使用。
构建 AuthMem-Bench，通过固定核心 claim 与下游任务、仅改变 source authority，系统评估写入阶段坍塌、下游越权行为和权威信息保留。
覆盖 7 种基于主流 agent-memory 系统的 consolidators 与 7 个 LLM backbones，49 个配置中有 48 个出现 authority collapse，说明问题具有普遍性。
在 action-grounded 评估中，缺少 authority metadata 的坍塌记忆带来 50.3% 的平均 unauthorized-action rate。
端到端实验表明，自动预测并持久化 authority labels 可将未授权动作率从 16.9% 降至 0.0%，且几乎不损害正常任务成功率。

llm_assessment.comment: AuthMem-Bench identifies a durable authorization failure at the memory boundary and offers a practical evaluation path for safer agent memory.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: AuthMem-Bench 揭示了记忆边界上的持久授权失效，并为更安全的智能体记忆提供了实用评测路径。
